hero_lead: We study earthquake hazard and risk in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq and the wider region, and turn that knowledge into safer buildings, better codes and better-prepared communities.
about_text: The Seismic Hazard Resilience Unit (SHRU) was established in 2025 at the College of Engineering, University of Duhok. Building on research carried out since 2015 on the seismic hazard of the Kurdistan Region and on the vulnerability of its masonry, hybrid and reinforced-concrete buildings in Duhok, Erbil and Sulaymaniyah, the unit works to make buildings and communities safer.

p3_text: Technical guidance for public bodies, designers and the community.

faults_title: Active faults in and around the Kurdistan Region
faults_text: The Kurdistan Region lies on the northeastern edge of the Arabian plate, where its collision with Eurasia forms the Zagros–Taurus fold-and-thrust belt. This map shows active faults from the GEM Global Active Faults Database together with the epicentres of the 2017 M7.3 Iran–Iraq border and the 2023 M7.8 Pazarcık earthquakes.
